prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1359; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a report that the insured vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant reports a wrist injury from the impact and is represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the reported date. Requested the police report and photographs from the scene.

Entry 3: Police report received. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and the responding officer's account matches the reported manner of impact.

Entry 4: Scene photographs reviewed. They show the points of contact and confirm several details of the reported collision, though they do not show the moment of impact itself.

Entry 5: Attempted to locate independent witnesses through the police report and the scene canvass. None were identified, so the account rests on the parties and the physical evidence.

Entry 6: Medical records received showing a wrist fracture. The kind of fracture and the force it implies are consistent with the reported crash.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a usual course, with follow-up visits tapering as the claimant improved. No earlier injury to the same body area appears in the records we have obtained so far.

Entry 8: Claimant's account was taken again through counsel. The description of the collision and the injury has stayed the same in every conversation so far.

Entry 9: Prior vehicle records were pulled. They show major damage to the same areas from an earlier accident that was never reported to us, and the current claim presents that damage as new.

Entry 10: Reviewed the overlap between the earlier damage and the current claim. It is not yet clear whether all of the claimed damage came from this impact. Nothing so far suggests the damage occurred before coverage began.

Entry 11: Referred to the supervisor for a decision on next steps. Further inquiry is needed on the prior damage and the extent of the current loss before any settlement discussion with counsel.
